title: New York Reports 932 Cyclosporiasis Cases as 'Explosive Diarrhea' Parasite Sweeps Across US
excerpt: The parasitic illness linked to contaminated produce has infected nearly 14,000 people nationwide, with New York among the hardest-hit states after Michigan.
body:
• New York has reported 932 confirmed cyclosporiasis cases through August 10, with 65 new cases in the latest weekly update alone
  • Nationally, the CDC reports 13,895 laboratory-confirmed cases across 34 states, with another 10,455 under investigation
  • Michigan leads with 12,485 confirmed cases; a multistate outbreak has been linked to recalled iceberg lettuce from central Mexico
  • The CDC recommends thorough washing of fresh produce and cooking food to 158°F to kill the parasite; the illness is treatable with antibiotics

New York State reported 65 additional confirmed cases of cyclosporiasis in its latest weekly update, bringing the total to 932 cases through August 10 as the parasitic illness — dubbed the "explosive diarrhea" parasite on social media — continues to sweep across the country.

The New York State Department of Health, which has been posting weekly updates every Wednesday through the end of August, reported 898 cases from May 1 through August 10, indicating the vast majority of infections have occurred during the summer months.

A National Surge

The outbreak extends far beyond New York. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention reported 13,895 laboratory-confirmed cases of cyclosporiasis acquired in the United States as of August 11, a sharp increase from 10,468 confirmed cases just a week earlier. An additional 10,455 cases may require further investigation.

Michigan has been the hardest hit, with 12,485 confirmed cases as of August 6. Federal health officials are investigating multiple outbreaks, including a multistate cluster linked to recalled iceberg lettuce sourced from central Mexico and distributed by Taylor Farms. New York is not among the states identified in that particular outbreak.

New York City alone has seen 553 reported cases diagnosed since May 1, according to the NYC Health Department — a three-fold increase compared to the same period in 2025.

What Is Cyclosporiasis?

Cyclosporiasis is a parasitic infection caused by Cyclospora cayetanensis, which targets the small intestine. The CDC describes its hallmark symptom as "watery diarrhea with frequent and sometimes explosive bowel movements." Other symptoms include stomach cramps, nausea, loss of appetite, bloating, fatigue, and low-grade fever.

Symptoms typically appear about a week after exposure but can surface anywhere from two days to two weeks later. If untreated, the illness can last from a few days to over a month, and symptoms may relapse after apparent recovery.

The parasite spreads through food or water contaminated with feces. Past US outbreaks have been linked to imported fresh produce including raspberries, leafy greens, basil, cilantro, and onions. It does not spread directly from person to person.

How to Protect Yourself

Health officials recommend several precautions:

  • Wash all fresh produce thoroughly under clean, running water
  • Cook food whenever possible — heating to 158°F (70°C) or higher kills Cyclospora
  • Practice regular hand washing, especially before eating
  • Be cautious with imported fresh produce during summer months

David O. Freedman, a professor emeritus of infectious diseases at the University of Alabama at Birmingham, told Healio that while the outbreak is widespread, the risk for healthy individuals remains relatively low. Hospitalization is "extremely rare in normal hosts," and treatment typically involves intravenous fluids and antibiotics. No deaths have been reported.

The CDC notes that the actual number of infections is likely higher than confirmed case counts, since not everyone who gets sick is tested for the parasite.
